body: With the new setup in #6025 the number of concurrent GPU workers is decided based on the available memory, but that information isn't printed anywhere.  I noticed that we're often getting 3 or 4 GPU workers, instead of the expected 6, I'm adding a print to show the available memory, to better understand the end result.  Also, reduce the GPU memory budget for each worker from 4 to 3 GiB, with the hope of getting slightly more concurrent workers on average.  If it doesn't cause too much resource contention we may even reduce to 2 GiB, same as the CUDA.jl tests, but I'll postpone that to a follow up PR if this works well for some time.

body:
> `CubedSphereConformalMapping` stored its ξ and η coordinates as whatever the branch that built them produced: ranges for a uniform mapping, `Vector{FT}` for a non-uniform one. Since those are type parameters, two otherwise identical cubed sphere grids had different types, and every kernel, model and solver specialized separately for each.
> 
> That is what made the cubed sphere simulation tests expensive. They are 72% and 81% compilation, and they build the same model twice, once per mapping. Grid size and halo size are already type parameters (`GridSize{Nx, Ny, Nz, Hx, Hy, Hz}`, src/Grids/abstract_grid.jl), so these grids agreed on everything except the four coordinate fields.
> 
> Collect all four into `Vector{FT}`. They are grid metadata, read by `on_architecture`, `Adapt.adapt_structure` and grid reconstruction, and never indexed inside a kernel, so the only effect is that the two mappings now share a specialization. A uniform mapping pays four small vectors per panel, about 264 bytes each here, in place of four ranges.
> 
> multi_region/cubed_sphere_simulation 12:08 -> 8:28 and multi_region/cubed_sphere_simulation_immersed 18:29 -> 11:40, with peak memory down from 3.5 to 2.8 GB and 7.1 to 5.7 GB. Measured against main those files started at 13:08 and 19:48. The `multi_region` and `tripolar_grid` suites pass.
title: Give uniform and non-uniform cubed sphere mappings one concrete type

body:
Following a suggestion by @glwagner , this PR adds `TimeOffset(parent_schedule, offset)`, a schedule that actuates when its parent does and once more at a signed time offset: after each parent actuation for `offset > 0`, before the next one for `offset < 0`. The time step is aligned so the model lands exactly on the offset time. This gives time derivatives (#5823) a deterministic snapshot time without predicting future steps.
